title: Python SDK: output contracts, stream chunking ergonomics, and retry guidance
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Deliver a cohesive Python SDK surface for typed response contracts (dataclasses first with pydantic interop), streaming chunk ergonomics, structured-output helpers, and clear retry semantics/examples. This ticket covers API shape, helper utilities, example recipes, and a compatibility shim to migrate existing projects that use raw dict responses.
acceptance_criteria: SDK exposes dataclass-driven response models with optional runtime pydantic validation
Streaming API yields typed incremental chunks that are easy to consume in sync and async contexts
Retry utilities documented with semantic examples (idempotency, partial-stream resumes, backoff defaults)
Migration guide and 3 example notebooks (simple chat, structured-json extraction, resumable streaming) added to examples/
Unit tests covering model parsing, streaming ordering, and retry edge cases included
API documentation pages drafted and linked from the console docs
notes: Context: multiple teams requested stronger typing for responses; prior PRs (ENG-5274, ENG-9021) introduced typed helpers but there is fragmentation across dataclass vs pydantic-first approaches.

Decision (2025-01-12): adopt dataclass-first models with an opt-in PydanticAdapter for runtime validation. Rationale: dataclasses are lighter (faster import time) and align with user code using attrs/dataclasses; pydantic remains important for strict runtime checks and custom validators.

Tradeoffs: dataclass-first means some advanced validation (regex, complex constraints) requires pydantic; we'll provide clear patterns and a small wrapper to convert dataclass -> pydantic.BaseModel and vice-versa.

Streaming ergonomics: choose generator/async-generator API that yields TypedChunk objects (dataclass) instead of raw dicts. Each chunk has three top-level fields: kind (text|delta|structured|meta), content, and cursor. This preserves ordering and allows clients to filter by "kind".

Retry semantics: for non-streaming calls, follow existing idempotency key behavior. For streaming requests, we will expose a resume_token in stream metadata; server-side support required (follow-up infra ticket). Without resume support, SDK will provide best-effort client-side reconnection with explicit warning to user when resume not possible.

Performance considerations: avoid heavy per-chunk validation by default. Provide two modes: 'fast' (no validation, returns dataclasses built from parsed JSON) and 'strict' (runs pydantic validation per assembled object). Default remains 'fast' with clear docs about tradeoffs.
Compatibility shim: expose from_raw_response(raw: dict) -> dataclass helper to aid migration. Also provide to_dict()/to_json() convenience on models.
Example skeletons will live in sdk/python/examples/typed_streams and be linked from README.
Security: structured-output helpers must not inadvertently eval or deserialize unsafe content. We'll only use json.loads and explicit field parsing; mark security_review_required below.

code_samples:
# dataclass-first model example
from dataclasses import dataclass
from typing import Optional

@dataclass
class ExtractedEntity:
    name: str
    confidence: float
    metadata: Optional[dict] = None

# parsing helper (fast mode)
raw = {'name': 'Helsinki', 'confidence': 0.93}
entity = ExtractedEntity(**raw)
# streaming consumer (async)
async for chunk in client.stream_chat(request, mode='fast'):
    if chunk.kind == 'structured':
        model_obj = ExtractedEntity(**chunk.payload)
        print('got partial entity', model_obj)
# strict validation using pydantic adapter
from redwood_sdk.models import PydanticAdapter
valid = PydanticAdapter(ExtractedEntity).validate(instance_dict)
